name: python-callshape-unaccepted-keyword-asks
desc: the headline case: `fetch` resolves, so every existence check passes, but the call passes `timeuot=` and the declaration two lines up accepts only url/timeout. The pre-edit file already defines fetch, so addInFileDefs folds it into the known set — which is what proves this ask comes from call-shape and not from the additive check

name: python-callshape-correct-keyword-clean
desc: the anti-vacuity control for the case above — byte-identical except the keyword is spelled right. A check that fires on both is worthless, so this is the fixture that fails if the comparison degenerates to 'any kwarg asks'

name: python-callshape-decl-takes-kwargs-clean
desc: the declaration takes **opts, so it accepts every keyword name and no call can disagree with it. Fails if the HasKwStar abstain is removed — the single largest false-positive source, since **kwargs passthrough is idiomatic

name: python-callshape-decorated-decl-clean
desc: a decorator may replace the callable with a wrapper accepting a different set (functools.wraps makes the visible signature a lie), so the accepted set is unknowable. Fails if the Decorated abstain is removed

name: python-callshape-keyword-only-param-accepted-clean
desc: parameters after a bare `*` are keyword-ONLY, which means they are the most keyword-callable parameters there are. Fails if pyKeywordParams treats the bare `*` as ending the accepted set instead of starting the keyword-only region — an inversion that would ask on every keyword-only API in the repo
old:
def fetch(url, *, timeout=1, retries=0):
    return url

name: python-callshape-positional-only-marker-keeps-later-params-clean
desc: `/` makes the parameters BEFORE it positional-only; the ones after are still keyword-callable. Paired with the -asks case below: this one fails if the positional_separator handling truncates or abstains the whole list, that one if it stops truncating at all

name: python-callshape-shadowing-import-in-file-clean
desc: an Edit, so the shadowing `from httpx import fetch` sits OUTSIDE the hunk and can only be seen by reading the pre-edit file. With two candidate fetches the call's target is unknowable, so the check must abstain. Fails if the import arm of pyNonDefBindings is removed, AND fails if the whole-file read is dropped — the hunk alone shows no import. Paired with the control below, whose hunk is byte-identical

name: python-callshape-no-shadow-control-asks
desc: the control for the shadowing case: byte-identical hunk, and a pre-edit file with the httpx import removed. It asks. That difference in outcome is what makes the shadow rule attributable to the FILE text rather than to the hunk

name: python-callshape-edit-adds-param-and-uses-it-clean
desc: the recurring-agent-move false positive: the same edit ADDS `timeout=10` to the signature and passes it. The on-disk signature is stale by exactly this edit, so comparing against it would ask on correct code. Fails if resolveDeclShape stops preferring the added text's declaration

name: python-callshape-edit-adds-param-and-typos-it-asks
desc: the other half of the case above, and its anti-vacuity pair: the edit rewrites the signature AND misspells the keyword. Comparing against the edit's OWN declaration still disagrees, so it asks. Without this, the added-text-precedence rule could be replaced with a blanket abstain and every fixture would stay green

name: python-callshape-removes-signature-line-clean
desc: a hunk that rewrites ONE line of a multi-line parameter list carries no whole `def` line, so the added-text path does not engage and the pre-edit declaration is stale. removesSignatureLine catches it from the removed text. Fails if that abstain is dropped — the MultiEdit shape of the add-a-param move, which the added-text rule alone does not cover

name: python-callshape-untouched-multiline-signature-asks
desc: the control for the case above: the same multi-line declaration, and a hunk that touches only the call. Nothing about the signature is stale, so the pre-edit declaration is authoritative and the bogus keyword asks. Without this pair, removesSignatureLine could be widened to 'abstain whenever anything is removed' and stay green

name: python-callshape-positional-only-passed-by-keyword-asks
desc: `def fetch(url, /, timeout=1)` rejects `fetch(url=...)` — `url` is a real parameter name that is nevertheless not keyword-callable. This is the fixture that fails if the `/` truncation is dropped, which is the direction that would let a genuine TypeError through

name: python-callshape-splat-plus-named-keyword-asks
desc: `fetch("u", bogus=1, **cfg)` — a `**splat` adds keywords, it never excuses an explicitly named one, so `bogus` must still be accepted. The first draft abstained on any splat-bearing call; the mutation harness exposed that as an abstention no fixture could fail, and this is the case that now pins the reach it was costing

name: python-callshape-edit-removes-the-declaration-clean
desc: the hunk DELETES `def fetch` and rewrites a call, so the added text carries no `def` line (the precedence branch never engages) while the pre-edit file still shows the old signature. Comparing against a declaration this edit is removing is meaningless — a call to a deleted def is the dangling-refs check's business. removesSignatureLine is what abstains, matching the deleted `def` line's own trimmed text; the parameter-line fixture reaches the same guard through a different shape, and this one is the whole-declaration case

name: python-callshape-edit-touches-decorated-signature-clean
desc: the false positive an adversarial review found: an Edit whose hunk is the `def` line of a DECORATED function. The hunk cannot show the `@retry` above it, so the added-text precedence branch would read the function as undecorated and compare against a signature a wrapper may have replaced. Every other decorator fixture is a Write, where the decorator is always visible, so none of them can reach this path

name: python-callshape-helper-named-like-a-builtin-still-asks
desc: the dynamic-binding markers are matched as identifiers, not as bare substrings. A file containing `def get_locals(...)` contains the text "locals(", and matching that as a substring set the file's dynamic flag and returned nothing for the WHOLE file — any helper ending in locals/globals/exec/eval silently switched off its own module. This fixture asks, so it fails the moment the boundary check is removed
